_____________________________________________________________________ Justice Tarlok Singh Chauhan, Judge(oral) Since common questions of law and facts are involved in all these cases, therefore, they are taken up together for hearing and are being disposed of by a common judgment.
1 Whether reporters of the local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

Yes. 
2 All these petitions have been filed under Section 29- A(4)(5) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 for extension .
of time of the mandate of the Arbitrator(s).

3 It was vide order dated 22.3.2012 that the Central Government, in pursuance to sub-Section (5) of the National Highways Act, 1954 (48 of 1956), (for short, "NHAI Act") of appointed Divisional Commissioner Shimla for the revenue Districts Shimla and Solan and Divisional Commissioner Mandi rt for the revenue districts of Bilaspur, Mandi and Kullu to be Arbitrator(s) for the purposes of said sub-Section and vested with all the powers under the NHAI Act within the local limits of their respective jurisdiction.

However, this Court is flooded with litigations of the instant kind,
where parties have been unnecessarily compelled to seek extension of time of the mandate of the Arbitrator(s) only because the Arbitrator(s) has no time to decide the lis before it.

4 I am informed at the Bar that as regards Divisional Commissioner, Shimla there are as many as 869 cases pending before it and as regards Divisional Commissioner, Mandi, it has whooping pendency of 2660 cases.
Some of these cases, I am informed, relate back to year 2015.

sentences.text:
One serious question that is bound to arise subsequently is that in case awards are enhanced, then which of .
the parties or persons can be fastened with liability to pay the interest on the enhanced amount which would alone run into several crores- would it be the Arbitrator or the authority acquiring the land i.e. NHAI or some other authority or person.
of 6
After all, it is not the case of either of the parties that either one of them is responsible for the delay in finalizing the rt proceedings before the Arbitrator(s).

7 It is pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner(s) that since the Divisional Commissioners, Shimla and Mandi are overburdened with revenue matters, in addition to routine administrative work and they have no time to decide these reference petitions.
The Divisional Commissioner otherwise also holds regular court being a quasi-judicial or the competent authority in cases pertaining to revenue, public premises, municipal etc.

8 It is suggested at the bar that it would be more appropriate in case serving or retired Additional District Judges or District Judges are conferred with these powers as was the case under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and now under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
. 
9 These suggestions appear to be meaningful given the fact that the acquisition proceedings in Kangra District have already commenced, for which district, there is probably no Divisional Commissioner notified by the Central Government of under Section 3(g)(5) of the NHAI Act.

10 It is only because the Divisional Commissioner i.e. rt the Arbitrator is overburdened that the claimants as also their lawyers are made to run from pillar to post and then they are kept waiting for a considerable period for the decision by the authority and when the decision is not rendered, then the helpless claimants have to approach this Court, which only adds to the litigations before the courts, which, in turn, are itself overburdened.
11

The issue is indeed extremely serious and, therefore, required to be deliberated by all the stake holders, more particularly, NHAI and Central Government because, as observed above, the Arbitrators so appointed probably do not have time to adjudicate these petitions or else there would not have been such a huge pendency of cases, that too, some of which relate back to nearly 8 years or more.

12 As regards the instant petitions, time for completing the arbitral proceedings in the all the cases is extended upto .
28.2.2024.
